subject: Private VPC observability: SIEM onboarding & evidence handoff
messages:
From: Tom Langston <tom.langston@novafinance.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.inference.com
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability handoff for private deployment (SIEM, traces, retention)

Hi Irene,

We're preparing for our Redwood Private VPC deployment and the security/audit team has asked for a clear handoff for observability: the expected log types exported, retention guarantees, SIEM mapping examples, and tracing hook snippets they can drop into their on-prem proxies. They'd like a single zip with representative samples we can hand to Splunk and our internal SOC.

Quick context: we're set to enter integration tests next week (09/06). Key asks from Audit:
- sample logs for request/response (access + inference metadata)
- mapping guidance for our SIEM (Splunk HEC example)
- how trace IDs propagate through the VPC/private agent and back to Redwood (examples in Go/Java)
- retention/rotation guidance and proof points for 90/365 day retention

Can Redwood provide an evidence bundle + short doc describing the trace hooks and recommended SIEM ingestion settings by 09/03? If you prefer, we can start with a short call.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Langston
Head of Infrastructure Security
Nova Finance
From: irene.choi@redwood.inference.com <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
To: Tom Langston <tom.langston@novafinance.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com, kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability handoff for private deployment (SIEM, traces, retention)

Tom —

Thanks for the clear list. We'll produce a curated evidence bundle and concise guidance for your SOC by EOD 09/03.

Plan:
- Marissa will assemble an "evidence bundle" with redacted sample logs and SIEM mapping examples (Splunk HEC + common field mapping).
- I'll draft the tracing hook snippets and a short note on how our agent propagates trace_id and parent_id across the VPC boundary.
- Kimberly will confirm acceptable retention language and provide the audit wording you can attach to your compliance package.

If you can share any constraints (no external S3 links allowed, must deliver via encrypted bundle on a ticket, etc.) let us know. Otherwise we'll upload a signed zip to the Drive link below and share an HS ticket for transfer.

Irene Choi
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

- evidence_bundle_novafinance_20270902.zip (contains: redacted access logs, inference metadata, example HEC event payloads)

Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability handoff — audit wording and retention confirmation

Tom — quick audit-focused note to include in the handoff package. Please feel free to excerpt this into your compliance binder: 

"Redwood Private (VPC) — Observability & Retention Statement (sample):
- Data export: Customers control outbound egress for telemetry. Redwood provides a signed evidence bundle with representative log samples and SIEM mapping on request.
- Retention guarantees: Redwood can commit to configurable retention for exported telemetry. Redwood-hosted ingestion (by customer choice) supports configurable retention windows; for customer-managed storage/export, retention is enforced by the customer storage solution. For contract-level commitments (90/365 days) we require a DPA addendum or managed-retention add-on; we will provide audit logs showing export timestamps and retention configuration during onboarding.
- Trace continuity: Trace IDs (header: X-Redwood-Trace-Id) are injected at the VPC agent boundary and propagated through the inference runtime as part of request metadata. Sample code snippets are provided in the tracehook_snippets.md file.

For Nova Finance: if you need an explicit contract clause, I'll work with Legal to produce a short audit wording we can sign.

—Kimberly Park
Director, Trust & Security, Redwood Inference
From: irene.choi@redwood.inference.com <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Re: Observability handoff for private deployment (SIEM, traces, retention) — final artifacts and transfer

Tom / Audit Team —

We're attaching the signed evidence bundle and the additional trace snippets you requested. Transfer method: we've placed the zip in a gated Drive folder and created HS ticket HS-118334 for encrypted delivery; alternatively we can deliver via your SFTP if preferred. Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-nova-evidence-samples (access has been granted to the audit@novafinance.com group).

Summary of artifacts included:
- evidence_bundle_novafinance_20270902.zip — redacted logs (access, inference metadata), Splunk HEC payload examples, ingestion checklist.
- siem_mapping_sample.json — field mappings and sourcetype suggestions.
- tracehook_snippets.md — short Go and Java examples showing header propagation and example trace stitching test case.
- audit_statement.txt (text) — retention and trace continuity language signed by Kimberly.

We recommend the following immediate validation steps for your SOC team:
1) Upload siem_mapping_sample.json to a test index in Splunk and validate sourcetype parsing for 1000 synthetic events.
2) Run the trace-stitching script in tracehook_snippets.md against a small batch of requests (we can run jointly).
3) Confirm export acceptance and retention policy in a POA (if you need 90/365 day contractual language, Kimberly will coordinate the addendum).

If you'd like, we can hold a 30-minute call 09/06 10:00 PT to walk through the artifacts; marissa and I will join.

Thanks — looking forward to integration tests.

Irene Choi
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachments: evidence_bundle_novafinance_20270902.zip, siem_mapping_sample.json, tracehook_snippets.md
